answer: There is one mark: a vertical stroke shaped like a meteg (here functioning as silluq, since a sof pasuq follows the word) under the gimel (ג), the first and only occurrence in the word. It sits below the tsere. No other accent or meteg marks appear on ח, נ or ו.
visible_evidence: The whole word חַגֵּנוּ: is visible, including its lower points, with the sof pasuq (:) to its left. Under ח is a hataf patach (a dash with two dots), and there is no vertical stroke under ח. ג has a dagesh and a tsere (two horizontal dots), and directly below the tsere is a clear separate vertical stroke, which is not a vowel stem or a sheva. נ has no lower marks. וּ has a shuruq. The next line's ink starts well below the stroke, so the stroke is not ink from the neighbouring line.
